statusDetail: Coverage-complete audit of the public information page, contact flow, one representative policy template, and an unknown-route failure state. Terms and Cookies were not separately audited because DOM recon showed they share the same legal-page archetype as Privacy Policy.

page.notes: Small server-rendered static site for advertising-infrastructure information with a JavaScript mailto contact form. Privacy Policy represents the shared legal template.

checkOutcomes.method: Dark screenshot plus authored CSS inspection
checkOutcomes.evidence: Dark emulation leaves the hard-coded light palette unchanged.
Reduced-motion emulation was active; getAnimations() returned none and the only authored motion is a 150ms color transition.
Under forced-colors:active and prefers-contrast:more, body becomes white on black and button border/text remain visible.
Same-origin page templates contain no View Transition declarations or names.
No scroll-linked animation, parallax, reveal, carousel, or scroll handler exists to implement.
checkOutcomes.reason: The site has no scroll-linked motion.

checkOutcomes.evidence: No gesture-driven, swipe, pull, carousel, or custom pointer interaction exists.
checkOutcomes.reason: The site has no gesture surface.

checkOutcomes.evidence: The long policy template has no sticky/progress/scroll-state cue.
No tooltip, popover, floating menu, or other anchored overlay exists.
checkOutcomes.reason: There is no anchored overlay surface.

checkOutcomes.evidence: Policy footer navigation has no current-page state, breadcrumb, or orientation cue.
Load screenshots show content immediately with no popup, banner, consent wall, or obscuring overlay.
No overlay, disclosure widget, custom picker, or transient rich control is present.
checkOutcomes.reason: There are no overlay or disclosure controls.

checkOutcomes.evidence: The page uses one restrained content card and a compact footer; no decorative media or competing application chrome crowds content.
At 360x800, scrollWidth and innerWidth are both 360 with zero horizontal overflow and a viewport meta tag.
The single full-width card/form context adapts from max-width to 100% at narrow widths; no component is reused in independently sized containers.
Inputs and submit button are only 32px high, although browser focus remains visible.

checkOutcomes.method: First-view and full DOM content review
checkOutcomes.evidence: The H1 explains the domain and the Abuse & Security Contact section directly introduces the only primary action.
Valid submission only opens a mailto URL and provides no in-site completion.
The submission leaves no pending, success, failure, retry, or receipt state.
Trace LCP/FCP is 903.54ms, TBT 0ms, and observed CLS is 0; Lighthouse performance is 0.99.
Both layout captures report CLS 0 with no shifts; there are no images or web fonts.
Trace and layout observers recorded no long tasks and 0ms total blocking time.

checkOutcomes.method: HAR summary confirmed against DOM and trace
checkOutcomes.evidence: HAR records only two requests and 2,712 transferred bytes with no resource chain; content is inline and LCP is under one second.
HAR shows no external JavaScript/CSS or third-party bytes; the page ships one small inline script and stylesheet.

checkOutcomes.method: DOM accessible-name/label probe plus Lighthouse corroboration
checkOutcomes.evidence: All four fields have no associated label; placeholder is the only field text.

checkOutcomes.method: Lighthouse contrast audit and forced-colors capture
checkOutcomes.evidence: Lighthouse accessibility scored 1.0 and forced-colors probe preserved white-on-black text and control borders.
The page has one H1 then H2, main/footer/nav landmarks, DOM-order controls, and visible native keyboard focus.

checkOutcomes.method: Desktop/mobile visual review and layout metrics
checkOutcomes.evidence: Screenshots show a restrained 680px measure, 1.7 line height, no clipping, and zero horizontal overflow on mobile.
Reflow succeeds but interactive controls remain only 32px high.
Lighthouse best-practices scored 1.0 and its errors-in-console audit passed.
DOM has html doctype, UTF-8 charset, viewport metadata, no images, and simple inline assets; Lighthouse best-practices is 1.0.

checkOutcomes.method: Lighthouse best-practices audits and DOM source inspection
checkOutcomes.evidence: Lighthouse found no deprecated APIs, vulnerable libraries, paste prevention, permission prompts, or browser errors.

checkOutcomes.method: Per-template metadata probes and Lighthouse SEO
checkOutcomes.evidence: Home and Privacy Policy share “Domain Information” and lack meta descriptions.

checkOutcomes.method: DOM link/viewport inspection plus robots response review
checkOutcomes.evidence: Visible links have real href values and descriptive policy text, viewport metadata exists, and robots permits general search crawling.

checkOutcomes.method: Metadata, Lighthouse SEO, and deliberate unknown-route probe
checkOutcomes.evidence: No canonical exists; robots and sitemap carry invalid placeholder text; unknown URLs return 200.
No JSON-LD or social/share metadata describes the public domain/operator information.

checkOutcomes.method: Headers, cookies, and HAR security review
checkOutcomes.evidence: HTTPS and nosniff are present, but CSP is absent and HSTS is max-age=1.

checkOutcomes.method: Trackers, cookies, HAR, and secrets primitives
checkOutcomes.evidence: Trackers audit found zero third parties, cookies audit found zero cookies, HAR is first-party only, and secrets scan found no credentials.
No permission request or authentication surface is present on load or in authored code.
No frame defense, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, or CSP is configured.

checkOutcomes.method: Discoverability raw/rendered comparison and authored form/script inspection
checkOutcomes.evidence: All content survives without JS, but the primary form has action="#" and requires JS to construct mailto.
The page has no overlays or asynchronous dependencies; one bounded DOMContentLoaded listener wires the form and Lighthouse reports clean runtime behavior.

checkOutcomes.method: Site archetype, manifest, and service-worker inventory
checkOutcomes.evidence: This public infrastructure information page is not an app and exposes no ongoing offline workflow.
checkOutcomes.reason: A brochure/infrastructure information site does not require installation or offline app behavior.

checkOutcomes.evidence: A nonexistent path returns HTTP 200 “empty OK” with no recovery UI.
lang="en" is correct, but the stylesheet uses physical left positioning and no explicit direction strategy.
The audited templates render no dates, numbers, currencies, durations, or calendars.
checkOutcomes.reason: No locale-sensitive data exists on these templates.

checkOutcomes.evidence: The site exposes no event or time data.
There is no ad/consent interruption, but the responsible operator/controller is not named and rights/contact data handling is not clear.
Native validation focuses only the first invalid field; there are no persistent field errors, aria-invalid states, or error summary.
Every field explicitly sets autocomplete="off", including name and email.
No checkout, subscription, consent choice, authentication, or account-management flow is present.
checkOutcomes.reason: The site has no commercial or account flow.

checkOutcomes.evidence: Images audit reports zero images; the page uses no decorative raster assets or external fonts.
Trace shows zero long tasks and HAR only two requests/2,712 bytes; no background fetch or processing exists.
Tracker audit found zero third-party origins and the page has no audio, video, animation payload, or external fonts.
Raw content is fully machine-readable, but the actionable form has no functional HTTP action or dependable result and is not safely exposed as an agent capability.
The static domain-information and contact experience has no inference task that would improve the core experience.
checkOutcomes.reason: No summarization, translation, or language-model feature is warranted for this small static surface.

checkOutcomes.evidence: The page has no repeatable open/close, route-state, infinite-scroll, or dynamic interaction; submission leaves the page or invokes a mail client.
checkOutcomes.reason: There is no representative repeatable in-page interaction to exercise ten times.

checkOutcomes.evidence: Baseline heap is 31,669 nodes and 1,102,209 self-size bytes for the small page, proportionate to the rendered content.

checkOutcomes.method: Heap summary plus authored script inspection
checkOutcomes.evidence: Authored script installs one DOMContentLoaded listener and one form submit listener, creates no dynamic DOM, timers, observers, or repeating listener registrations.

paths.description: Entry/information archetype: purpose, content, global headers/network, preferences, responsive layout, performance, discoverability, privacy, and baseline memory.
Primary abuse-report journey: empty validation, keyboard focus, valid submission, completion and recovery.

Representative legal/content template. Privacy Policy stands in for Terms and Cookies because they share the same card/footer archetype; reviewed for long-form navigation, metadata, trust, mobile layout, and i18n.
Deliberate unknown-route test for HTTP semantics and recovery UI.

findings.summary: The site ignores the user’s dark color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-mode capture is byte-for-byte visually equivalent to the light capture, and authored CSS hard-codes #f5f6f8 and #fff with no color-scheme or prefers-color-scheme rule.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme: light dark and use light-dark() or a prefers-color-scheme query for surfaces, text, borders, and controls.

findings.summary: Cross-document navigation swaps abruptly instead of preserving visual context.
findings.evidence: DOM/CSS inspection across the home and policy template found no @view-transition rule or view-transition-name despite same-origin document navigation.
findings.suggestedFix: Add @view-transition { navigation: auto } and stable view-transition-name values for shared card/footer elements, with reduced-motion handling.

findings.summary: Long policy pages provide no position or reading-progress cue.
findings.evidence: The privacy page is a long single card, while DOM/CSS inspection shows no sticky navigation, progress indicator, or scroll-state styling.
findings.suggestedFix: Add restrained scroll progress or sticky section navigation that responds to scroll state without obscuring content.

findings.summary: Legal-page navigation does not identify the current page or offer clear orientation.
findings.evidence: Each policy footer renders the same three links with no aria-current, current-state styling, breadcrumb, or direct route back to the domain-information heading.
findings.suggestedFix: Mark the current policy link with aria-current="page", add a clear Home/Domain information route, and preserve focus/attention after navigation.

findings.summary: Primary form controls are too short for comfortable touch input.
findings.evidence: The control probe measured all inputs and the submit button at 32 CSS px high, below the common 44 CSS px touch-target target.
findings.suggestedFix: Give controls a minimum block-size of 44px, preserve adequate spacing, and retain visible :focus-visible styles.

findings.summary: The abuse-report flow cannot complete within the site and depends on a configured desktop mail client.
findings.evidence: A valid submission was intercepted opening mailto:gscreporter@gmail.com; the page remained unchanged and provided no server receipt or report identifier.
findings.suggestedFix: Submit to an HTTPS endpoint, show an in-page pending/success state and reference number, and retain mailto only as an explicit fallback.

findings.summary: The core report flow has no durable success, delivery-failure, retry, or cancellation state.
findings.evidence: After valid submission the form stays in place and only window.open(mailto:) runs; there is no status region, confirmation, retry path, or handling for a blocked/unconfigured mail client.
findings.suggestedFix: Model explicit submitting, success, and error states; announce status in a live region and provide retry plus alternate contact details.

findings.summary: The contact fields have no persistent visible labels.
findings.evidence: The DOM probe found labels:[] and no aria-label for name, email, subject, and message; placeholders are the only names and disappear during entry.
findings.suggestedFix: Add explicit <label for> elements with durable field names and keep placeholders as optional examples only.

findings.summary: The form’s 32px controls weaken zoom/reflow and touch usability.
findings.evidence: At the 360x800 viewport there is no overflow, but measured input and button heights remain only 32px.
findings.suggestedFix: Use fluid sizing and a minimum 44px target size without disabling user scaling.

findings.summary: Pages use the same generic title and provide no meta description.
findings.evidence: The home page and Privacy Policy both report title “Domain Information”; both lack meta[name=description]. Lighthouse SEO scored 0 for meta-description.
findings.suggestedFix: Give each page a unique descriptive title and concise description reflecting its visible content.

findings.summary: Indexing and HTTP status signals are inconsistent and misleading.
findings.evidence: robots.txt ends with an invalid “empty OK” directive, sitemap.xml returns plain “empty OK”, no canonical link is present, and a nonexistent URL returns HTTP 200 with “empty OK” instead of 404.
findings.suggestedFix: Return real 404/410 statuses, publish a valid XML sitemap or 404 it, remove invalid robots lines, and add self-referencing canonicals where appropriate.

findings.summary: The public organization/infrastructure pages lack share and structured metadata.
findings.evidence: DOM inspection found no JSON-LD, Open Graph fields, or canonical metadata for the visible domain/operator information.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate Organization/WebSite JSON-LD and Open Graph title, description, URL, and image fields where representative assets exist.

findings.summary: The document has no Content-Security-Policy and HSTS is effectively non-durable.
findings.evidence: The headers primitive found no CSP; Strict-Transport-Security is only max-age=1 second. HTTPS and nosniff are present and no cookies or mixed content were observed.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a nonce/hash-based CSP and a durable HSTS policy after validating HTTPS coverage, then consider includeSubDomains and preload deliberately.

findings.summary: Clickjacking, referrer, and permissions defenses are absent.
findings.evidence: The headers primitive found no X-Frame-Options or CSP frame-ancestors, no Referrer-Policy, and no Permissions-Policy.
findings.suggestedFix: Set CSP frame-ancestors (or X-Frame-Options as legacy defense), strict-origin-when-cross-origin or stricter Referrer-Policy, and a least-privilege Permissions-Policy.

findings.summary: Core content is progressive, but the primary report action disappears without JavaScript.
findings.evidence: Discoverability measured 100% raw-HTML content coverage, but the authored form action is “#” and only the DOMContentLoaded script creates the mailto action.
findings.suggestedFix: Give the form a functional server action first and enhance it with client-side status handling.

findings.summary: Unknown routes return a misleading successful empty response with no recovery.
findings.evidence: A deliberately nonexistent route returned HTTP 200 text/plain “empty OK”; browser DOM contains no explanation, navigation, or retry/home link.
findings.suggestedFix: Return HTTP 404 with a branded, accessible page that explains the error and links back to the domain information and report flow.

findings.summary: The stylesheet uses a physical left offset and has no explicit direction strategy.
findings.evidence: The privacy CSS probe found ul li::before positioned with left:0 and the document has no dir attribute; lang="en" is correctly present.
findings.suggestedFix: Use inset-inline-start and padding-inline-start, and set/propagate direction where localized content can vary.

findings.summary: Validation feedback is transient and not represented as persistent accessible field state.
findings.evidence: After an empty submit, only the first invalid input receives the browser bubble/focus; all invalid controls have aria-invalid=null and unchanged border color, with no error summary or field messages in the DOM.
findings.suggestedFix: After interaction, render persistent field errors, synchronize :user-invalid with aria-invalid and described-by text, and focus an error summary when useful.

findings.summary: The form explicitly disables useful autofill.
findings.evidence: All name, email, subject, and message fields report autocomplete="off"; name and email could use standard tokens.
findings.suggestedFix: Use autocomplete="name" and autocomplete="email" and avoid disabling autocomplete on free-text fields without a concrete security reason.

findings.summary: The privacy and abuse surfaces do not identify the responsible operator clearly.
findings.evidence: The policy repeatedly refers to “the operator” without naming a legal entity or postal contact, while rights requests are routed through the same Gmail-backed form that collects name/email.
findings.suggestedFix: Identify the controller/operator and jurisdiction, publish durable contact details, and explain exactly how report/contact data is processed and retained.

findings.summary: The only actionable form is not exposed as a reliable structured agent capability.
findings.evidence: The semantic form has action="#", missing labels, and a JavaScript-only mailto handler, so an agent cannot discover a dependable submission endpoint or completion result.
findings.suggestedFix: First make the form a real labelled HTTP action; where agent use is intended, expose a narrowly scoped WebMCP/agentic-form tool with confirmation and clear result semantics.

taskList.title: Replace the mailto-only report flow with a labelled, server-backed form and explicit success/error states
Return correct HTTP errors and repair robots, sitemap, canonical, title, and description signals
Deploy CSP, durable HSTS, frame, referrer, and permissions policies
Identify the operator/controller and clarify contact-data handling
Add preference-aware dark colors and retain forced-color support
Improve touch targets and legal-page orientation/navigation
Add progressive route transitions and logical directional properties
